h: Beyond The Big One: Rides Worth Hunting Down
p: Everybody knows about The Big One, but the Pleasure Beach is packed with other rides that have their own devoted fans. Icon, which opened in 2018, was the UK's first double launch roller coaster and gives you two bursts of speed as it twists around the park. Valhalla is a Viking-themed indoor water ride with fire, ice and a soaking you won't forget in a hurry, so pack a change of clothes if you're brave enough. Avalanche sends you down a bobsleigh-style track that's more fun than it looks.

For something gentler, Wallace and Gromit's Thrill-O-Matic is a cheerful dark ride through scenes from the famous Aardman films, perfect for mixed ages. The park also has quieter classics dotted about between the big hitters, which helps break up a long day for anyone who isn't up for constant thrills.

Start early and head for the rides that matter most to your group before queues build. Plan a decent lunch break somewhere shady or under cover, and keep water topped up on hot days. Agree a meeting point in case anyone gets separated, as the park's winding layout can be confusing at first.

Blackpool Pleasure Beach has its own railway station just over the road, which makes arriving by train surprisingly easy. Next door you'll find Sandcastle Waterpark for an indoor splash day, and South Pier is a short walk along the prom. Hop on a tram and you can be at the Tower and Central Pier in minutes, or come back in the autumn when the famous Illuminations light up the seafront for miles.
